title: Industrial radiography equipment, sealed sources and storage practice questions
description: Practice questions on NRC industrial radiography equipment, locking, survey instruments, leak tests, installations, storage and records (10 CFR Part 34).

questions.question: Under 34.20(b)(1), which item must the label attached to each radiographic exposure device bear?

options.A: The name of the radiographer to whom the device is assigned
options.B: The licensee's name, address, and telephone number
options.C: The date of the last leak test of the sealed source
options.D: The date of the last quarterly inventory

questions.explanation: The licensee must ensure each radiographic exposure device has "a durable, legible, clearly visible label" that includes the "Licensee's name, address, and telephone number."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.20, Performance requirements for industrial radiography equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Licensee's name, address, and telephone number.

questions.question: Under 34.20(b)(3), when is modification of radiographic exposure devices, source changers, source assemblies and associated equipment allowed?

options.A: When the Radiation Safety Officer approves the modification in writing
options.B: When the equipment has been out of service for more than 3 months
options.C: When the modification is made at a permanent radiographic installation
options.D: When the design of any replacement component would not compromise the design safety features of the system

questions.explanation: Modification "is prohibited, unless the design of any replacement component,including source holder, source assembly, controls or guide tubes would not compromise the design safety features of the system."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.20, Performance requirements for industrial radiography equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: unless the design of any replacement component,including source holder, source assembly, controls or guide tubes would not compromise the design safety features of the system

questions.question: Under 34.20(c)(3), when must the safety plugs or covers on the outlet fittings, lock box and drive cable fittings of each radiographic exposure device be installed?

options.A: During storage and transportation
options.B: Only while a radiographic exposure is being made
options.C: Only at temporary job sites
options.D: Only when the device is inside a permanent radiographic installation

questions.explanation: These fittings "must be equipped with safety plugs or covers which must be installed during storage and transportation to protect the source assembly from water, mud, sand or other foreign matter."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.20, Performance requirements for industrial radiography equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must be equipped with safety plugs or covers which must be installed during storage and transportation

questions.question: Under 34.20(c)(4)(i), what words must the label attached to or engraved on each sealed source or source assembly carry?

options.A: CAUTION—RADIATION AREA
options.B: WARNING—HIGH RADIATION
options.C: DANGER—RADIOACTIVE
options.D: RADIOACTIVE MATERIAL—DO NOT HANDLE

questions.explanation: Each sealed source or source assembly must have "a durable, legible, visible label with the words: “DANGER—RADIOACTIVE.”"

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.20, Performance requirements for industrial radiography equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: a durable, legible, visible label with the words: “DANGER—RADIOACTIVE.”

questions.question: Under 34.20(c)(7), what must be attached to the outermost end of the guide tube during industrial radiography operations?

options.A: A safety plug that is removed only after the exposure is complete
options.B: A survey instrument probe
options.C: An exposure head or similar device designed to prevent the source assembly from passing out of the end of the guide tube
options.D: A lock box with the key removed

questions.explanation: The rule requires that "An exposure head or similar device designed to prevent the source assembly from passing out of the end of the guide tube must be attached to the outermost end of the guide tube during industrial radiography operations."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.20, Performance requirements for industrial radiography equipment (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: An exposure head or similar device designed to prevent the source assembly from passing out of the end of the guide tube must be attached to the outermost end of the guide tube during industrial radiography operations.

questions.question: Under 34.21, what is the maximum exposure rate limit for storage containers and source changers at 1 meter from any exterior surface, with the sealed source in the shielded position?

options.A: 0.1 millisieverts (10 millirem) per hour
options.B: 2 millisieverts (200 millirem) per hour
options.C: 0.5 millisieverts (50 millirem) per hour
options.D: 1 millisievert (100 millirem) per hour

questions.explanation: The limits are "2 millisieverts (200 millirem) per hour at any exterior surface, and 0.1 millisieverts (10 millirem) per hour at 1 meter from any exterior surface with the sealed source in the shielded position."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.21, Limits on external radiation levels from storage containers and source changers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: 0.1 millisieverts (10 millirem) per hour at 1 meter from any exterior surface with the sealed source in the shielded position

questions.question: At a temporary job site, when does 34.23(a) require a radiographic exposure device and/or its container to be kept locked, with any key removed?

options.A: Only while it is being transported between job sites
options.B: Only overnight and on weekends
options.C: Only when the Radiation Safety Officer is away from the job site
options.D: When it is not under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant

questions.explanation: The device and/or its container "must be kept locked (and if a keyed-lock, with the key removed at all times) when not under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant except at permanent radiographic installations as stated in § 34.51."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.23, Locking of radiographic exposure devices, storage containers and source changers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must be kept locked (and if a keyed-lock, with the key removed at all times) when not under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant

questions.question: Which statement matches 34.23(b) on keeping sealed source storage containers and source changers locked?

options.A: They must be kept locked when containing sealed sources, except inside a permanent radiographic installation
options.B: They must be kept locked when containing sealed sources, except when under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant
options.C: They must be kept locked only while they are in a transporting vehicle
options.D: They must be kept locked only when they are empty

questions.explanation: Storage containers and source changers "must be kept locked (and if a keyed-lock, with the key removed at all times) when containing sealed sources except when under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.23, Locking of radiographic exposure devices, storage containers and source changers (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Storage containers and source changers must be kept locked (and if a keyed-lock, with the key removed at all times) when containing sealed sources except when under the direct surveillance of a radiographer or a radiographer's assistant.

questions.question: Under 34.25(a), what range must the required radiation survey instrumentation be capable of measuring?

options.A: From 0.02 millisieverts (2 millirems) per hour through 0.01 sievert (1 rem) per hour
options.B: From 0.1 millisieverts (10 millirems) per hour through 2 millisieverts (200 millirems) per hour
options.C: From 0.05 millisieverts (5 millirems) per hour through 0.1 sievert (10 rem) per hour
options.D: From 1 millisievert (100 millirems) per hour through 1 sievert (100 rem) per hour

questions.explanation: The instrumentation "must be capable of measuring a range from 0.02 millisieverts (2 millirems) per hour through 0.01 sievert (1 rem) per hour."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.25, Radiation survey instruments (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: must be capable of measuring a range from 0.02 millisieverts (2 millirems) per hour through 0.01 sievert (1 rem) per hour

questions.question: Under 34.25(a), where must the licensee keep sufficient calibrated and operable radiation survey instruments?

options.A: Only at the licensee's main office
options.B: At each location where radioactive material is present
options.C: Only at permanent radiographic installations
options.D: Only in each vehicle that carries a radiographic exposure device

questions.explanation: The licensee "shall keep sufficient calibrated and operable radiation survey instruments at each location where radioactive material is present to make the radiation surveys required by this part and by 10 CFR part 20 of this chapter."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.25, Radiation survey instruments (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: shall keep sufficient calibrated and operable radiation survey instruments at each location where radioactive material is present

questions.question: Under 34.25(b)(1), besides calibration at intervals not to exceed 6 months, when must each required radiation survey instrument be calibrated?

options.A: After every battery change
options.B: After each use at a temporary job site
options.C: Before use on each day the instrument is to be used
options.D: After instrument servicing, except for battery changes

questions.explanation: Each required instrument must be calibrated "At intervals not to exceed 6 months and after instrument servicing, except for battery changes".

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.25, Radiation survey instruments (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: At intervals not to exceed 6 months and after instrument servicing, except for battery changes;

questions.topic: Leak testing, sealed sources and inventory
questions.question: Under 34.27(b), who must perform the opening, repair, or modification of any sealed source?

options.A: Any certified radiographer employed by the licensee
options.B: The licensee's Radiation Safety Officer, because of that position
options.C: Persons specifically authorized to do so by the Commission or an Agreement State
options.D: A radiographer's assistant working under a radiographer trainer

questions.explanation: "The opening, repair, or modification of any sealed source must be performed by persons specifically authorized to do so by the Commission or an Agreement State."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.27, Leak testing and replacement of sealed sources (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The opening, repair, or modification of any sealed source must be performed by persons specifically authorized to do so by the Commission or an Agreement State.

questions.topic: Leak testing, sealed sources and inventory
questions.question: A licensee receives a sealed source from another licensee. Under 34.27(c)(3), what lets the licensee use it before having it tested for leakage?

options.A: A label on the source with the words “DANGER—RADIOACTIVE”
options.B: A certificate from the transferor that shows it has been leak tested within 6 months before the transfer
options.C: An entry for the source in the transferor's utilization log
options.D: A record that the source was counted in the transferor's last quarterly inventory

questions.explanation: "Unless a sealed source is accompanied by a certificate from the transferor that shows that it has been leak tested within 6 months before the transfer, it may not be used by the licensee until tested for leakage."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.27, Leak testing and replacement of sealed sources (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Unless a sealed source is accompanied by a certificate from the transferor that shows that it has been leak tested within 6 months before the transfer, it may not be used by the licensee until tested for leakage.

questions.topic: Leak testing, sealed sources and inventory
questions.question: A leak test reveals 185 Bq (0.005 microcurie) of removable radioactive material. Under 34.27(d), what must the licensee immediately do with the equipment involved?

options.A: Withdraw it from use and have it decontaminated and repaired or disposed of in accordance with Commission regulations
options.B: Keep using it under the continuous surveillance of a radiographer until the next test
options.C: Wipe the outer surface and return it to service
options.D: Move it to a permanent radiographic installation and keep using it there

questions.explanation: Such a result "must be considered evidence that the sealed source is leaking. The licensee shall immediately withdraw the equipment involved from use and shall have it decontaminated and repaired or disposed of in accordance with Commission regulations."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.27, Leak testing and replacement of sealed sources (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The licensee shall immediately withdraw the equipment involved from use and shall have it decontaminated and repaired or disposed of in accordance with Commission regulations.

questions.topic: Leak testing, sealed sources and inventory
questions.question: An evaluation of a depleted uranium (DU) shielded exposure device finds that its S-tube is worn through. What does 34.27(e) state?

options.A: The device may be used again once the S-tube is cleaned
options.B: The device may be used only at a permanent radiographic installation
options.C: The device may not be used again
options.D: The device may be used again after it passes a second DU contamination test

questions.explanation: "Should the evaluation reveal that the S-tube is worn through, the device may not be used again."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.27, Leak testing and replacement of sealed sources (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Should the evaluation reveal that the S-tube is worn through, the device may not be used again.

questions.question: Under 34.31(a), when must the licensee perform visual and operability checks on survey meters, radiographic exposure devices, transport and storage containers, associated equipment and source changers?

options.A: Once a week while the equipment is in storage
options.B: Only after the equipment arrives at a new temporary job site
options.C: Only after each radiographic exposure
options.D: Before use on each day the equipment is to be used

questions.explanation: The licensee "shall perform visual and operability checks" on this equipment "before use on each day the equipment is to be used to ensure that the equipment is in good working condition, that the sources are adequately shielded, and that required labeling is present."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.31, Inspection and maintenance of radiographic exposure devices, transport and storage containers, associated equipment, source changers, and survey instruments (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: before use on each day the equipment is to be used to ensure that the equipment is in good working condition, that the sources are adequately shielded, and that required labeling is present

questions.question: Which is one of the options 34.33(a) gives for each entrance used for personnel access to the high radiation area in a permanent radiographic installation?

options.A: A conspicuous visible warning signal by itself
options.B: A radiographer's assistant posted at the entrance
options.C: A locked door whose key is held by the Radiation Safety Officer
options.D: Both conspicuous visible and audible warning signals to warn of the presence of radiation

questions.explanation: Each such entrance must have either an entrance control described in the rule or "Both conspicuous visible and audible warning signals to warn of the presence of radiation."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.33, Permanent radiographic installations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Both conspicuous visible and audible warning signals to warn of the presence of radiation.

questions.question: An alarm at a permanent radiographic installation is operating improperly and has been labeled as defective. Under 34.33(b), on what condition may the facility continue to be used during the 7-day repair period?

options.A: The licensee implements the continuous surveillance requirements of § 34.51 and uses an alarming ratemeter
options.B: The Radiation Safety Officer approves continued use in writing
options.C: Only radiographers, and not radiographer's assistants, work in the installation
options.D: The visible signal alone is tested before each exposure

questions.explanation: "The facility may continue to be used during this 7-day period, provided the licensee implements the continuous surveillance requirements of § 34.51 and uses an alarming ratemeter."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.33, Permanent radiographic installations (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The facility may continue to be used during this 7-day period, provided the licensee implements the continuous surveillance requirements of § 34.51 and uses an alarming ratemeter.

questions.question: Under 34.35(d), what must the licensee do with the transport package containing licensed material in the transporting vehicle?

options.A: Keep it in the passenger compartment
options.B: Keep it under the direct surveillance of a radiographer's assistant for the whole trip
options.C: Lock and physically secure it in the vehicle
options.D: Keep it unlocked so it can be checked during the trip

questions.explanation: "The licensee shall lock and physically secure the transport package containing licensed material in the transporting vehicle to prevent accidental loss, tampering, or unauthorized removal of the licensed material from the vehicle."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.35, Labeling, storage, and transportation (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The licensee shall lock and physically secure the transport package containing licensed material in the transporting vehicle

questions.question: Under 34.67, in what units must leak test results for sealed sources and devices containing DU be stated?

options.A: Millisieverts (millirem) per hour
options.B: Becquerels (microcuries)
options.C: Grays (rads)
options.D: Counts per minute

questions.explanation: For leak test records, "The results must be stated in units of becquerels (microcuries)."

source.title: eCFR: 10 CFR 34.67, Records of leak testing of sealed sources and devices containing depleted uranium (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The results must be stated in units of becquerels (microcuries).
